title: Image-only source holdings: resolved work and edition identities
method: Used the PDF skill for read-only source identification. No PDF was created, edited, re-exported, downloaded, OCRed or page-rendered.

Matched current SHA-256 identities against exact-hash acquisition/source records. Read existing text/OCR excerpts and saved title/copyright/contact images. Holdings metadata dates were not used as edition authority.

For Hughes–Cresswell title/copyright/endpoints and the Mac Lane–Moerdijk final index leaf, decoded original embedded page rasters in memory with pypdf/Pillow. This used no PDF page renderer and wrote no source/image files.

The no-opening-text state did not mean unreadable or unidentifiable. All23 PDFs were structurally readable in the input inventory, and all 33 current physical copies rehashed to their recorded identities.

Full extent means the identified complete work/report/chapter manifestation is supported by the stated acquisition/endpoint evidence. It does not certify an independently checked uninterrupted page sequence or a complete mathematical review.

Both report endpoint checks are now complete: DAIMI PB-429 ends at printed121 in physical122; BRICS RS-94-12 ends at printed144 with its back catalogue in physical74. This identifies extent, not complete interior fidelity.
Two UMD derived PDFs were traced to the exact same quoted PostScript response hash and separately failed conversion records. They are non-source artifacts, not parser failures or acquired papers.

Only image-only-source-identities.md and .json were written. No manuscript, bibliography, source, original inventory or register file was changed. No tests, builds, acquisitions or new renders were run.

A subsequent header scan found one additional no-opening-text identity with no extension. This task added only that requested 24th row: a blank Cornell conversion intermediate, separately classified from the two proven UMD conversion failures.
decisive_distinctions: Mac Lane–Moerdijk: copyright/title evidence gives 1992 and first-printing line 9…1; the PDF metadata's 1999 filename/title is not edition evidence.
Hughes–Cresswell: first published 1996, explicitly reprinted 1998 on physical page 4; this holding is not identified as the first printing solely by its standard bibliography year.
Vardi–Wolper: 18-page author preprint dated August 15, 1985, not the ten-page LICS 1986 proceedings facsimile.
Clarke–Emerson: 66-page fuller author manuscript, not the twenty-page 1982 LNCS chapter or its 2008 reprint.
Büchi and Elgot: 1959 Michigan technical-report precursors, distinct from the 1960/1961 journal versions.
Sistla–Clarke: all three copies have 1985 JACM bytes, including the one named STOC 1982-index-linked.
The three Monk files are Chapters 12, 13 and 14 from Handbook of Boolean Algebras, Volume 2, 1989; the three whole volumes are separate byte identities.
The two UMD PDFs each contain only one derived page after Ghostscript failed on a >-prefixed PostScript response declaring 115 pages. Neither is the underlying paper.

The extensionless Cornell file is a blank one-page intermediate, not Halpern's 31-page survey. The successful .pdf companion has different bytes; unlike the UMD artifacts, no failure exit code was established for this intermediate.

remaining_extent_or_version_gaps.gap: The fuller manuscript is identified. Its exact issue date/relationship to each original chapter revision is not established by the 2004 scanner date or local1981 filename; do not cite it as the published 20-page body.
